Class SlotItemLooks

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.SlotItemLooks
public final class SlotItemLooks extends Object
What a slot's item draws as on a container screen (7.4.0): a mod says, per slot and per frame, which ItemAnimation the item draws with and how far through it is, and the slot draws that in place of the item. The slot's count and durability bar, its highlight and tooltip, and what a click does stay vanilla's. 
static final Transition OPENING = Transition.of(250, Easing.EASE_OUT);
static final ItemAnimation OPEN = ItemAnimation.OPEN_LID.posed(t -> new ItemAnimation.Pose(1f - 0.25f * t, 0f, 0f));

SlotItemLooks.declare("mymod:open_boxes", (screen, slot, stack) -> {
    Object key = boxKey(slot);
    if (key == null) return null;
    return OPEN.at(OPENING.toward(key, isOpen(key)));
});
  • Asked every frame for every slot the screen draws with an item, vanilla's and created ones alike, on every container screen. null leaves the slot to the next look, and with none, to vanilla.
  • Timing is the mod's, through a Transition keyed by something that outlives the screen (the container, not the Slot), so a screen that opens in place of another picks a finished animation up where it stood.
  • Several mods: looks are asked in id order and the first that answers draws.
  • Another stack drawn in the slot's place (an open bundle's model, 7.5.0): ItemAnimation.AS_IS.swapped(stack -> openBundle(stack)).at(1), or any animation swapped, so it animates and swaps at once.
  • A look that throws is logged once and skipped from then on.
  • To draw on the slot rather than in place of its item, see SlotDecorations.

Declare from your client initializer: looks freeze with every other declaration.
